items.title: Ghostty 1.4
items.content:
Release notes for Ghostty 1.4.0, released on October 27, 2026.

Ghostty 1.4.0 is a major release that includes large performance and

memory improvements, a 100% complete Kitty graphics implementation including

animation and relative placements (the first non-Kitty terminal to do so),

SSH integration improvements, and hundreds more improvements and fixes

This release features 7 months of work with changes from

172 contributors over 2,889 commits . Thank you to all the contributors,

maintainers, community moderators, translators, packagers, and users

who each helped make this release possible.

These release notes are painstakingly and lovingly hand-crafted

by human Ghostty maintainers, including the full changelog. They take

a combined 16+ hours to write, so please enjoy. 🥰

Note: I requested CVEs for the above advisories weeks ago, but GitHub

hasn't assigned them yet. If/when they're assigned, I will update the

Ghostty 1.4 supports macOS 27 (Golden Gate). Most of the work was

Ghostty 1.4 remains fully compatible with prior macOS versions back to

and including macOS 13 (Ventura). See the

Ghostty 1.3.1 works on macOS 27, but it has some of the visual issues

PRs: #13943 #13939 #13935 #13934 #13893 #13933 #13389

These were the last major features of the Kitty graphics protocol that

Programs that display animated images with the Kitty protocol, such as an

animated GIF shown with kitten icat , now animate in Ghostty instead of

showing a single still frame. Frame transmission, composition, and playback

control are all supported, and animations pause while the terminal isn't

visible. Relative placements let a program position one image relative to

another image's placement, so the child image moves along with its parent.

We also did a full conformance pass against the specification and Kitty

itself, fixing dozens of behavioral differences. For example, images now

scroll with text inside scroll regions ( #4323 ), retransmitting an image

ID replaces the old image ( #6711 ), and invalid image data now gets an

error response instead of silence, which could leave clients hanging. The

full list is in the terminal capabilities section.

Kitty graphics are faster, too. Image payloads are now parsed in bulk

with SIMD instead of one byte at a time, making large image transfers

about 16x faster to parse in our benchmarks (64 MiB of image data,

x86_64 Linux), and drawing images costs much less per frame.

Our Kitty graphics implementation now covers 100% of the published

specification, making Ghostty (and libghostty) the first terminal

PRs: #13264 #13473 #13240 #13245 #14130 #14137 #14138

Ghostty now transparently compresses scrollback that isn't visible,

reducing the physical memory those pages use by 70% to 90% for typical

text-heavy history. Compression only runs while the terminal is idle and

pages are decompressed on demand when you scroll back or search, so it

has no measurable impact on I/O throughput.

Thanks to compression, the default scrollback limit has been raised from

10 MB to 50 MB per terminal. On platforms that support compression, a

full scrollback still generally uses less physical memory than the old

Compression lowers resident (physical) memory, not virtual memory, so

look at resident memory when measuring it. It is currently available on

Beyond scrollback, memory usage is lower in many places:

PRs: #13209 #13220 #13226 #13227 #13537 #13827 #13587

There are performance improvements across the board in Ghostty 1.4

that yield significant gains compared to prior Ghostty versions.

The biggest win came from a surprising discovery: on macOS, the kernel

caps every read from a pty at about 1 KiB no matter how large the read

buffer is. Previously, Ghostty processed each read as it arrived, so per-read

overhead was paid every kilobyte, and the program writing output sat

blocked while we parsed. Ghostty now drains the pty on one thread while

parsing on another, raising end-to-end I/O…

items.content_ko: 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있다. 필자는 사이버보안 인식 캠페인 덕분에 인식은 충분히 높아졌다고 말하면서도 현재 상황은 지속 불가능하다고 주장한다. 근거로는 제로데이 취약점의 급증, 사전 공지나 마케팅 목적의 취약점 공개, 공개 절차의 붕괴, 수년째 실패해 온 패치 관리를 든다. 원문에는 AI 기업들이 누가 더 많은 범죄를 저지르는지 경쟁하고 오픈소스 커뮤니티에 대한 DoS 형태로 보호 상품을 판다는 비판도 담겨 있다. 글은 취약점이 실제로 환경에서 위험한지 평가하고 공격 표면을 찾는 데 여전히 상당한 자원과 시간이 든다는 대목에서 끊긴다.

items.title: AI bots flooded 2023 UK government consultation on disposable vapes ban
items.content:
It is thought to have been the first coordinated attempt to use AI to derail health policymaking in the UK. Photograph: Tim Parker/Getty Images

It is thought to have been the first coordinated attempt to use AI to derail health policymaking in the UK. Photograph: Tim Parker/Getty Images

AI bots flooded 2023 UK government consultation on disposable vapes ban

Three-quarters of all responses were machine-generated in failed attempt to stop bill from passing into law, research finds

AI bots flooded a government consultation with tens of thousands of fake responses in a failed attempt to stop the UK’s ban on disposable vapes.

Three-quarters of all the responses to the 2023 consultation on the tobacco and vapes bill were machine-generated, in what is thought to be the first coordinated attempt to use AI to derail health policymaking in the UK.

The attempt to manipulate the outcome of the consultation was disclosed on Tuesday in research published in the journal Tobacco Control by the health policy experts Dr Nason Maani, from the University of Edinburgh, and Prof Anna Gilmore, of the University of Bath.

The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) used bot-detection methods to identify that 90,835 of the 118,756 responses it received, 76%, were submitted by bots.

All but two of those 90,835 automated responses answered the same question in the “smoke free generation” consultation, in which they opposed Rishi Sunak’s Conservative government’s plan to ban disposable vapes. The submissions were “often duplicated many times and sent at high frequency from a small number of IP addresses”, the DHSC said.

The bombardment “appears to be the first documented instance of large-scale automated interference in a formal public health policy consultation”, the researchers said.

Maani added that while this attempt was identified, “the threat is that future campaigns become harder to catch, and what we can’t catch, we don’t know about. Such campaigns are a threat because they raise the possibility of a handful of powerful interests looking like a mass movement.”

The DHSC excluded the 90,835 automated responses from its decision-making. Keir Starmer’s Labour government inherited the tobacco and vapes bill in 2024 and passed it into law, including the ban on businesses selling or supplying disposable vapes.

Caroline Cerny, the deputy chief executive of Action on Smoking and Health, said: “Evidence that AI bots have been used to swamp a Department of Health consultation is deeply concerning.

“Given the tobacco industry’s history of seeking to undermine public health regulation, we need to be alert to the risk that technological advances can be used to further commercial interests around health policy and put safeguards in place.

“Decisions that affect public health must be based on sound evidence and expertise, not manipulated response numbers.”

More than 6m vapes and pods discarded weekly in UK despite single-use ban, study finds

Azzurra Moores, the associate director for information ecosystems at the thinktank Demos, described the attempt to derail the ban as “pretty alarming”.

“Public consultations are one of the main ways government opens up its decision-making, so any interference with them is a serious concern,” she said. “These findings are pretty alarming: if a consultation can be swamped like this, it stops telling policymakers what the public actually thinks and undermines trust in the process.

“This is a problem without easy answers. Every barrier that keeps bots out also makes it harder for real people to take part, and AI makes fake responses far harder to spot. Interference can adapt faster than departments can update their checks. Better screening and more transparency will help, but there’s no single fix.”

The DHSC said its “robust controls” identified the attempt to influence the consultation.

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-99115 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fill in FileSysIdentifier in FS_POSIX_I
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99115 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fill in FileSysIdentifier in FS_POSIX_INFORMATION smb2_get_info_filesystem() reports 56 bytes for FS_POSIX_INFORMATION, that is the whole of FILE_SYSTEM_POSIX_INFO, but never assigns FileSysIdentifier. Those eight bytes go to the client as they are found in the response buffer. The buffer is zeroed on allocation, so a standalone request leaks nothing. A compound request can leak: the offset of the next response is advanced by the length pinned for the previous one, so a reply that was written into the buffer and then dropped in favour of the short error response of smb2_set_err_rsp() stays there, and the next reply is laid over it with only the header cleared. Report the file system id statfs() returned, which is what the field is for. FileSysIdentifier is __le64 and f_fsid is a pair of ints, so assemble the value first, val[0] as the low half, and convert it on the way out. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:32.347Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99115

items.summary_ko: Linux 커널 ksmbd의 smb2_get_info_filesystem()은 FS_POSIX_INFORMATION 응답에서 FileSysIdentifier 필드를 채우지 않아, 응답 버퍼에 남아 있던 8바이트가 클라이언트에 그대로 전달될 수 있다. 단독 요청에서는 버퍼가 0으로 초기화되어 노출되지 않지만, compound 요청에서는 이전 응답의 잔여 데이터가 노출될 수 있다. 수정 방향은 statfs()가 반환한 파일시스템 ID를 채우는 것이다.
items.content_ko: 본문은 취약점 원인을 설명한다. FS_POSIX_INFORMATION 응답은 56바이트 전체를 보고하지만 FileSysIdentifier는 할당되지 않는다. compound 요청에서는 다음 응답의 오프셋이 이전 응답의 길이를 기준으로 진행되며, 쓰여진 뒤 짧은 오류 응답으로 대체된 응답의 데이터가 버퍼에 남는다. 이후 응답은 헤더만 지워진 상태로 그 위에 덮어써진다. 수정안은 statfs()가 반환한 파일시스템 ID를 보고하는 것이다. FileSysIdentifier는 __le64이고 f_fsid는 int 두 개이므로, val[0]을 하위 32비트로 두고 값을 먼저 조합한 뒤 변환해 전달한다. CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA)이며 원격 악용 가능성은 False로 표기되어 있다. 공개일은 2026-10-28이다.

items.title: US Government is hiding a secret court ruling about how it spies on Americans
items.content:
Two Democratic senators who have long overseen US intelligence say the Trump administration is illegally withholding a secret court’s findings from Congress until lawmakers renew a program that lets federal agents read Americans’ communications without a warrant.

Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September.

The program, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), lapsed in June after Congress failed to renew it, though collection continues under the court’s March approval. The administration’s own public documentation says rulings like this one are reviewed for public release “within 180 days of issuance.” That window closed September 13, even as intelligence officials press lawmakers to reauthorize the program by the end of the year.

Wyden, the longest-serving member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, and Schiff, the former chair of its House counterpart, say the administration owes Congress an explanation for the delay, and the names of the officials responsible, by November 6.

“If this administration won’t follow this simple statutory directive,” the senators told Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Attorney General Todd Blanche in a demand letter obtained exclusively by WIRED , “it is unclear why Congress or the American people should trust this administration to follow any of the other legal limits to Section 702.”

Outside Congress, Demand Progress and 22 other civil liberties and government accountability groups on Monday urged congressional leaders to refuse to reauthorize Section 702 “while the administration actively withholds legally mandated information about how the surveillance program operates.” Signatories range from the American Civil Liberties Union to the conservative-backed Project for Privacy and Surveillance Accountability.

The Trump administration has already been pressed, and has promised, to release the ruling. In April, senators Tom Cotton and Mark Warner, the Intelligence Committee’s Republican chair and Democratic vice chair, pressed the administration to release it within 15 days so it could inform the Senate’s debate. In July, asked in writing whether he would commit to declassifying it by the 180-day deadline, Blanche replied, “Yes.”

Warner “has been clear that he supports transparency with regard to Section 702,” his communications director, Rachel Cohen, tells WIRED. Neither former director of national intelligence Tulsi Gabbard nor Bill Pulte, who briefly replaced her as acting director, “were responsive,” Cohen says, “but Senator Warner expects that DNI Clayton will declassify the opinion, consistent with the bipartisan letter and as required by law.”

Cotton’s office did not respond to a request for comment. The White House, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and the US Justice Department did not answer questions WIRED sent Friday about the delay.

Clayton, who is legally responsible as director of national intelligence for declassifying the ruling, has made no such promise. Asked before his July confirmation whether he would ensure the opinion was public before Congress voted on reauthorization, he wrote only that the government was “working arduously to expeditiously declassify” it and had made the full opinion available to lawmakers.

items.summary_ko: 오리건주 와이든 상원의원과 캘리포니아주 시프 상원의원은 트럼프 행정부가 영장 없이 미국인 통신을 들여다볼 수 있게 하는 프로그램을 재승인할 때까지 비밀 법원의 판단을 의회에 제출하지 않고 있다고 주장했다. 외국정보감시법원(FISC)은 7개월 전 미국인 메시지 검색 필터가 법이 요구하는 승인·사유 기록·기록 보관 없이 작동한다며 문제를 제기했지만, 이후 1년 연장을 승인했다. 해당 판결은 아직 공개되지 않았으며, 행정부 자체 기준으로 정해진 공개 검토 기한(9월 13일)도 지났다고 한다.
items.content_ko:
의회의 정보위원회를 오랫동안 감독해 온 민주당 상원의원 두 명은 트럼프 행정부가 FISC(외국정보감시법원)의 판단을 의회에 불법적으로 보류하고 있다고 주장했다. 대상은 외국정보감시법(FISA) 제702조에 따른 감시 프로그램으로, 연방 요원이 영장 없이 미국인의 통신을 열람할 수 있게 한다. 이 프로그램은 6월에 재승인되지 못해 실효되었지만, 3월에 받은 법원 승인에 따라 수집은 계속되고 있다.

FISC는 7개월 전 정보 분석관이 가로챈 데이터에서 미국인의 메시지를 꺼낼 때 쓰는 검색 필터에 문제를 제기했다. 법이 요구하는 승인, 서면 사유, 기록이 갖춰지지 않았기 때문이다. 그럼에도 법원은 감시를 1년 더 승인했다. 판결은 공개된 적이 없다. 행정부의 공개 문서에는 이런 판결을 '발행 후 180일 이내' 공개 검토한다고 적혀 있으며, 그 기한은 9월 13일에 끝났다. 정보 당국은 연말까지 프로그램 재승인을 의회에 촉구하고 있다.

items.title: A fast and secure tar parser for the Rust ecosystem
items.content:
Starting with 0.13 1 , uv uses tar-codec to parse source distributions.

tar-codec is roughly twice as fast as our previous tar implementation ( astral-tokio-tar ) while

also reducing uv's exposure to parser differentials and other security risks.

This blog post is about tar-codec itself: what it is, and what compelled us to build and optimize

it. Read on if you, too, would like to know too much about tar archives.

What follows is an extended digression on the tar format. If all you care about is tar-codec ,

As a Python packaging tool, uv is in the business of resolving and installing Python packages. uv

requests installable distributions from various sources (principally package indices like PyPI )

and installs them on the user's behalf. This is how you go from uv add urllib3 to something you

can actually import and use in your own Python codebase.

Installable distributions come in two primary forms:

"Built" 2 distributions, also known as bdists or (most commonly) wheels , are essentially

ZIP archives containing structured metadata and a fixed layout. Installers handle these by (more

or less) plopping their contents into the right destination directory.

Many people think that bdist is short for "binary distribution," since wheels often contain

compiled native code. This one common way to use wheels, but wheels can also contain pure Python.

They're just another (and frequently better) way to package and install a distribution.

distributions, a source distribution is essentially 3 just a rollup of a source tree's

By definition, source distributions execute arbitrary code at installation time. This makes them

very powerful, but brittle (missing build tools or dependencies) and also a security risk (an

attacker who controls the sdist can run code without the user needing to import anything).

Wheels are generally produced by running a build backend on a source distribution. Examples of

that include uv's own uv_build , maturin , and flit .

Consequently, at a bare minimum, a Python package installer needs to understand at least two

different archive formats: ZIP for wheels, and tar for sdists.

We've already talked a bit before about ZIPs on the Astral blog, and we'll certainly be talking

about them again soon enough. But today we'll be focusing on tar.

It's fair to ask: why does uv want a new tar parser?

In short: security and performance, but mostly security.

Up until 0.13, uv used astral-tokio-tar for its tar operations, including both parsing and

spurred us into looking more into our compression and archive handling stack, where we found

Many of these boiled down to differentials that could cause a full parser

desynchronization 4 : given an identical tarball, uv , pip , and other package tooling

could be made to see different contents for the same package distribution. We found this

particularly concerning in the context of archives that would appear "safe" to an index (like PyPI)

but could extract dangerously when parsed by an installer like uv or pip .

This could the take the form of an "append" differential (where the attacker can append new files or

new contents to existing files for a specific victim parser), or even a "full" differential (where

the attacker can fully separate the extraction contents for each parser):

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a…

items.title: Starlink-Observation geht über Online-Werbung
items.content:
It was translated with technical assistance and editorially reviewed before publication.

Infrastruktur für personalisierte Online-Werbung wird systematisch für Angriffe mit Spyware genutzt , hat das Citizen Lab der Universität Toronto Mitte Oktober aufgedeckt (“AdFection“, für Infektion über Werbung). Als wichtiges Bindeglied zwischen der Werbebranche und Anbietern von Staatstrojanern fungiert demnach das israelische Unternehmen Discover-Tech. Nun ist bekannt geworden, dass Discover-Tech so viel Reklame an Starlink-Nutzer adressiert hat, dass es der weltweit zweitgrößte Werbekäufer in diesem Segment ist, in 105 Ländern sogar der größte.

Das hat TrendAI festgestellt. Der Bericht der IT-Sicherheitstochter Trend Macros nennt Discover-Tech allerdings nicht beim Namen, sondern spricht von „Shadow-Earth-79”. Reuters meldet nun , dass mit dieser Bezeichnung Discover-Tech gemeint sei; das hätten sechs nicht namentlich genannte Quellen bestätigt. TrendAI hat die Identifikation gegenüber Reuters auch nicht in Abrede gestellt. heise online hat Discover-Tech zu einer Stellungnahme eingeladen.

Laut den Erhebungen TrendAIs ist „Shadow-Earth-79” in 49 Ländern der größte Käufer von Online-Reklameflächen insgesamt (nicht nur Starlink-Anschlüsse). In Ungarn und Israel liegt der Marktanteil sogar über 90 Prozent, in Ägypten, Aserbaidschan, Venezuela und Katar zwischen 61 und 78 Prozent. Besonders verdächtig: Unter den Zielländern sind auch sanktionierte Gebiete, für die sich westliche Werbetreibende gemeinhin nicht interessieren, wie Jemen, Libyen, Südsudan, Syrien und Venezuela, sowie Regionen mit Reisewarnungen.

Als größten Käufer von Werbeflächen bei Starlink hat TrendAI Steelhouse ausgemacht. Dieser Käufer hat im 90 Tage langen Beobachtungszeitraum über 38 Prozent aller Reklame vermittelt, die auf Geräten, die über Starlink online gehen, angezeigt werden. Steelhouse war der Name eines Adtech-Unternehmens, das in MNTN aufgegangen ist. MNTN ist, so wie Starlink-Betreiber SpaceX, in Texas zu Hause. heise online hat MNTN um Stellungnahme ersucht.

Zweitgrößter Käufer mit 12,9 Prozent Anteil ist „Shadow-Earth-79”. Auffallend ist, dass der Marktanteil fast beim Fünffachen das Marktanteils am allgemeinen Werbetraffic liegt. „Shadow-Earth-79” bietet also besonders häufig und hoch auf Starlink-Nutzer. Bei Steelhouse liegt der Starlink-Marktanteil nur beim 2,2-fachen des Allgemeinen Adtraffic-Anteils.

In einem längeren Beobachtungszeitraum, von Juni 2024 bis Juni 2026, war „Shadow-Earth-79” sogar Marktführer bei Starlink-fokussierter Reklame in 105 Ländern. Dazu zählt auch Deutschland, wo die israelische Firma fast jede dritte auf Starlink-verbundenen Geräten angezeigte Werbefläche ersteigert hat.

In mehreren Ländern hat TrendAI ausgemacht, dass der Fokus nicht bloß auf Starlink-Nutzern schlechthin liegt, sondern auf Regierungsdiensten, deren Geräte über Starlink online gehen. Der Verdacht ist, dass es Discover-Tech bei der Ersteigerung von Werbeplätzen nicht um den Vertrieb von Produkten oder Dienstleistungen geht, sondern um Datenernte.

Im Zuge der üblichen Versteigerung von Reklameflächen erfahren Werbevermittler wertvolle Daten wie Aufenthaltsort, IP-Adresse, Autonomous System Number, Gerätetyp und Bildschirmauflösung „Verknüpft mit Werbe-ID, Klickverfolgung und Aufenthaltsverlauf kann die zusammengeführte Information dazu genutzt werden, umfassende Verhaltensprofile von Anwendern zu erstellen”, verdeutlicht TrendAI. Werbung, und damit auch in Werbung versteckte Malware, kann dann entsprechend zugeschnitten werden. Den Vorwurf des Citizen Labs, Discover-Tech habe darauf aufbauend gezielt Spyware verbreitet, wiederholt der Bericht nicht; zu einer solchen Feststellung sind die von TrendAI gesammelten Daten nicht geeignet.

items.title_ko: Starlink 사용자 겨냥 온라인 광고가 스파이웨어 공격 경로로 악용
items.summary_ko: Citizen Lab이 10월 중순 공개한 'AdFection' 보고서는 개인화 광고 인프라가 스파이웨어 공격에 체계적으로 쓰이고 있다고 밝혔다. TrendAI 보고서는 이 과정에서 이스라엘 기업 Discover-Tech가 Starlink 사용자 대상 광고를 세계에서 두 번째로 많이 구매했고, 105개국에서는 가장 많이 구매했다고 분석했다. 보고서는 이 기업을 'Shadow-Earth-79'로 지칭했으며, Reuters는 익명 소식통 여섯 명을 근거로 두 이름이 같은 기업을 가리킨다고 보도했다.
items.content_ko: Citizen Lab은 토론토 대학교 연구팀으로, 맞춤형 온라인 광고 인프라가 스파이웨어 감염 경로로 쓰이고 있다는 점을 'AdFection'이라는 이름으로 공개했다. 이 과정에서 Discover-Tech가 Staatstrojaner 공급업체와 광고 업계를 잇는 핵심 역할을 한다고 전해진다. TrendAI는 Trend Micro의 IT 보안 자회사로, 보고서에서 이 기업을 직접 언급하지 않고 'Shadow-Earth-79'라고 불렀다. Reuters는 이것이 Discover-Tech를 가리키며 여섯 명의 비공개 소식통이 이를 확인했다고 보도했다. TrendAI는 이 식별에 이의를 제기하지 않았다. 원문 보도에 따르면 Shadow-Earth-79는 49개국에서 온라인 광고의 최대 구매자이며, 전 세계적으로는 두 번째로 큰 구매자다. heise online은 Discover-Tech에 입장을 요청했다.

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-99114 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: initialize FileSystemControlFlags in FS
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99114 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: initialize FileSystemControlFlags in FS_CONTROL_INFORMATION smb2_get_info_filesystem() reports 48 bytes for FS_CONTROL_INFORMATION, that is the whole of struct smb2_fs_control_info, but never assigns FileSystemControlFlags. Those four bytes go to the client as they are found in the response buffer. The buffer is zeroed on allocation, so a standalone request leaks nothing. A compound request can leak: the offset of the next response is advanced by the length pinned for the previous one, so a reply that was written into the buffer and then dropped in favour of the short error response of smb2_set_err_rsp() stays there, and the next reply is laid over it with only the header cleared. ksmbd does not implement quota tracking, so report no control flags. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:31.576Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99114
items.title_ko: [CVE-2026-99114] Linux 커널 ksmbd: FS_CONTROL_INFORMATION의 FileSystemControlFlags 미초기화로 정보 노출 가능
items.summary_ko: Linux 커널 ksmbd의 smb2_get_info_filesystem()은 FS_CONTROL_INFORMATION 응답에서 FileSystemControlFlags를 초기화하지 않아, 응답 버퍼에 남아 있던 4바이트가 클라이언트로 전달될 수 있다. 단독 요청에서는 노출되지 않지만 compound 요청에서는 노출될 수 있다. ksmbd는 쿼터 추적을 구현하지 않으므로 수정안은 제어 플래그를 보고하지 않는 것이다.
items.content_ko: FS_CONTROL_INFORMATION은 구조체 전체인 48바이트를 보고하지만 FileSystemControlFlags는 할당되지 않는다. 원인은 compound 요청에서 이전 응답 길이를 기준으로 다음 응답 오프셋이 진행되는 방식이다. 쓰였다가 smb2_set_err_rsp()의 짧은 오류 응답으로 대체된 데이터가 버퍼에 남고, 다음 응답은 헤더만 지워진 상태로 그 위에 쓰인다. ksmbd가 쿼터를 추적하지 않기 때문에 제어 플래그는 0으로 보고하는 것이 맞다고 기술되어 있다. CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA)이며 원격 악용 가능성은 False다. 공개일은 2026-10-28이다.

items.title: Four Months of Zig
items.content:
It has been about four months since I returned to Zig after being absent for a few years. In this time, I have written some software in Zig and reengaged with the community, online and in person. I decided to share some of that experience, including what I have liked about Zig so far and what I haven't. I'll include some comparisons to Rust along the way since that was my previous go-to language.

The first project I started in Zig was snurl . It is a library for interacting with the smallnet (Gemini, Finger, Gopher, Spartan, and such). My goal has been to provide an alternative to curl for the smallnet, with similar testing and fuzzing requirements but on a smaller scale. I wanted to roughly follow TigerStyle insofar as it made sense for the project.

Something I ran into early on was that the fuzzer didn't actually work. When getting excited about fuzzing in my last post, I didn't realize that the feature had not yet been completed. This isn't surprising, considering Zig's status, but it was disappointing, especially since the fuzzer is demonstrated in the generated main.zig file provided by zig init .

After this, I wrote a two programs which I have not published yet. The first is a small TUI typer racer. It was simpler than I expected to get a minimum version working so far. The second is an n-body simulator with stellar evolution using raylib.

The most exciting opportunity in the last few months was the chance to go to a local Zig Day. I learned of Zig Day Seattle occurring on Lobsters on August 20th. I was ecstatic to learn that there was a Zig Day in my area. Then I saw Andrew Kelley would be there and became more excited.

Zig Days are local meetups where people interested in Zig hang out, work on their projects together, and talk about Zig. For this Zig Day, I decided to work on snurl. A friend, Evin Yulo also decided to attend.

The event itself occurred in the Bothell library, moved there from the Bellevue library after so many people signed up that capacity was overwhelmed. Having the creator of Zig at the event will do that.

I love the format of these Zig Days and I'm glad they are a part of the community. Since they are run by local groups, it gives the whole Zig community a more interconnected feeling. It's a way to interact with other people who are interested in Zig in person. And, in this case, the creator of Zig itself.

I got the chance to talk with other programmers about their projects. Hopefully some ideological cross-pollination occurred that will make all our projects stronger. I ended up working on snurl with evin, who started work on integrating Zig's standard library TLS implementation as alternative backend.

I also briefly talked with Andrew Kelley. I hope Zig's built-in fuzzing gets fixed sometime soon!

Ryan Hendrickson wrote an excellent article outlining more of the events of that day from his perspective if you want more details.

I will definitely be attending Zig Day Seattle again in the future. I may even head down to Portland to catch one before the next local one comes around. I enjoy the opportunity to connect with other people interested in Zig and its values.

I love anyzig . I've had to use zig master and 0.16.0 for different projects, and anyzig has made that doable.

Unfortunately, it breaks outside of directories without a build.zig.zon , meaning if you have tooling that requires a zig command to work, it can only occur in project directories. This breaks autoformatting for my one-off Zig scripts. Maybe a default zig version could be provided in that case.

I know it frustrates some people, but I love the fact that you have to pass IO and allocator parameters to functions in Zig.

I'll start with allocators, since they've been around longer. For each Zig function you have to accept an explicit allocator parameter. This is different from most programming languages which either use a default allocator that may be changed globally or one changed by a local context (see Odin).

items.title: Solar Panels Are Now Producing So Much Power That They’re Leaving Nuclear Plants in the Dust: "Solar is now the engine of the power transition."
items.content:
As the world struggles to access oil as a consequence of the US war on Iran, the scramble for alternative forms of energy has become a mad dash. And contrary to the energy future some have imagined , the hunt for new power sources has supercharged the solar trade — leaving even nuclear power way back in the rearview mirror.

According to new reporting by the BBC , photovoltaics will account for 10 percent of the world’s power generation by the end of 2026, a threshold which will see solar energy officially surpass nuclear fission.

As professor of energy and climate policy at the University of Oxford Jan Rosenow told the British broadcaster, “solar is now the engine of the power transition.”

Compared to nuclear energy generation — which has stayed largely flat over the past 26 years globally — the publication notes the volume of solar energy being generated has exploded, increasing some 2,700 times over across the same period.

Much of the solar energy boom can be traced back to China, where massive supply is driving down the cost of photovoltaics to unprecedented lows. Though plenty of US-based startups have emerged with the goal of reviving the nuclear energy sector, their efforts to commercialize fission seem to be going nowhere fast.

In fact, the cost of nuclear construction projects in the US have skyrocketed over recent decades, defying conventional norms around infrastructure, which hold that complex energy builds should get cheaper as scale increases.

For the rest of the world, cheap solar power is increasingly becoming a lifeline, both in the literal day-to-day sense, and as a way to decouple from the long-standing oil economy.

As Rosenow told the BBC , the issue going forward is no longer one of access to alternative energy, but in balanced development of infrastructure for underdeveloped and overexploited nations.

“The bigger question,” Rosenow says, “is no longer whether solar grows, but whether our power systems and institutions can keep up.”

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-99113 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: zero the FS_OBJECT_ID_INFORMATION buffe
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99113 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: zero the FS_OBJECT_ID_INFORMATION buffer before filling it in smb2_get_info_filesystem() reports 64 bytes for FS_OBJECT_ID_INFORMATION, that is the whole of struct object_id_info, but writes only 46 of them: - objid[] is 16 bytes, and when the volume UUID is not available only sizeof(stfs.f_fsid) (8) bytes are copied into it; - extended_info.version_string[] is STRING_LENGTH (28) bytes, and only strlen("1.1.0") (5) bytes are copied into it. The response buffer is zeroed on allocation (kvzalloc() in smb2_allocate_rsp_buf()), so for a standalone request the remaining 31 bytes are zero. In a compound request they need not be. The offset of the next response is advanced by the length pinned for the previous one, so if a preceding command wrote its reply into the buffer and then failed, smb2_set_err_rsp() pins only the short error response and the next reply lands inside the area that has already been written. Only the header is cleared there: memset((char *)rsp_hdr, 0, sizeof(struct smb2_hdr) + 2); The client then receives up to 31 bytes of a response it was not meant to see, including one that failed with an access denied error. Clear the structure before filling it in. As a side effect version_string is now NUL terminated. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:30.767Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99113

items.summary_ko: ksmbd의 smb2_get_info_filesystem()은 FS_OBJECT_ID_INFORMATION 응답 구조체를 64바이트로 보고하지만 일부 필드만 채운다. 볼륨 UUID가 없으면 objid에는 f_fsid 8바이트만 복사되고, version_string에는 “1.1.0”(5바이트)만 복사된다. compound 요청에서는 이전 응답의 잔여 데이터가 남아 클라이언트에 전달될 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 응답 버퍼는 할당 시 kvzalloc()으로 0으로 초기화되므로 단독 요청에서는 나머지 바이트가 0이다. 그러나 compound 요청에서는 이전 명령이 응답을 쓴 뒤 실패하면 smb2_set_err_rsp()가 짧은 오류 응답만 기록하고, 다음 응답이 이미 쓰인 영역 안에 놓이게 된다. 이때 헤더만 지워지므로 이전 데이터가 남아 클라이언트에 전달된다. 본문은 클라이언트가 최대 얼마만큼의 데이터를 받는지 설명하는 대목에서 끊긴다.

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: “No human at the helm”: Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses. Owners of AI-run firms would evade liability for “reckless” AI, US Rep. Comer says.
items.content:
A Delaware proposal to let companies be operated by AI agents would help the firms’ human owners evade legal responsibility for reckless and harmful actions taken by the AI, US Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) told Delaware Governor Matt Meyer in a letter yesterday.

Comer, chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, told Meyer that the committee “seeks assistance obtaining documents related to your state administration’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity to be known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC).”

Comer said the proposal is ripe for abuse. “We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives,” Comer’s letter said.

Comer suggested he may propose a federal law that would limit states’ regulatory authority. He said the committee’s probe of Delaware’s plan would “inform possible federal legislative efforts including proposals to appropriately limit state AI regulatory initiatives.” Citing the Oversight Committee’s “jurisdiction to study intergovernmental relationships including those of states,” Comer asked for documents related to development of the proposal and potential AI safety risks.

AI-run companies could operate in just about any industry except banking. “An AIC may have any lawful purpose, regardless of whether for profit, except for the business of banking,” according to a draft bill that may be submitted to the Delaware state legislature.

The draft bill says AI agents could be “designated to manage the business and affairs, and to conduct the business, of the AIC.” The bill proposes a “regulatory sandbox” that would exist for 30 months to test the idea. Allowing AI-run companies would bring more revenue via taxes and fees to Delaware, which is already a top destination for business entities of all sizes.

“The answer is to wrap AI in legal form”

In July 2026, Delaware’s Secretary of State Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez co-wrote an op-ed in Fortune announcing the proposal. The op-ed said that “nothing in the law of several states clearly prevents an AI agent from operating a company with no human at the helm,” and that states should develop legal frameworks for autonomous software that is able to contract, pay suppliers, and make transactions with no human involvement.

“The answer is not to try to prohibit the activity; any effort to do so is just as unlikely to succeed as the technology and its enablers are likely to push the boundaries of the law,” the op-ed said. “The answer is to wrap AI in legal form. Give an autonomous system a recognizable legal identity and you make it legible to law. You create a deﬁned target to which responsibility and damages can attach. You make the agent’s conduct visible, traceable, and accountable.”

The op-ed explained how an AI-run company will shield humans from legal liabilities:

A Delaware AIC will be a separate legal entity whose day-to-day aﬀairs are managed by an AI agent rather than a person. At the agent’s direction, the AIC can sue and be sued in its own name, hold and dispose of property, and incur obligations. It has a single member, a person or an entity, responsible for keeping the AIC adequately capitalized, and the AIC must keep a log of its activities. That member is shielded from the AIC’s debts, except where it fails to capitalize the company or uses it to commit fraud or a willful violation of law.

Under the proposed law, the “member” is an individual or a corporation that would fund the AI-run company and benefit from any profits, but designate an AI agent to manage the actual business. items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-99112 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: cls_flower: validate mask pointer a
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99112 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: cls_flower: validate mask pointer after nla_next() fl_set_enc_opt() iterates the key's nested tunnel-option attributes with nla_for_each_attr() while advancing a single mask pointer via nla_next() at the bottom of each loop, so the mask cursor is driven by the number of key attributes rather than by the mask's own attributes. The nla_ok() added by commit c96adff956191 ("cls_flower: call nla_ok() before nla_next()") only validates the mask pointer that was just consumed; the pointer produced by nla_next() is used by the next iteration (fl_set_geneve_opt() and siblings) without any validation. The mask's nested attributes are validated with NL_VALIDATE_LIBERAL, which merely warns on trailing bytes that do not form a complete attribute. A mask carrying one valid attribute plus 1-3 residue bytes (or a non-aligned attribute length making msk_depth negative) therefore reaches the next iteration with msk_depth != 0, so neither the !msk_depth check in fl_set_enc_opt() nor the !depth check in the per-type helpers fires. nla_type() then reads past the mask payload and nla_parse_nested_deprecated() iterates with an nla_len taken from those bytes, reading well beyond the mask attribute (KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds read in __nla_validate_parse from fl_change()). Validate the advanced mask pointer as well: when the mask is not legitimately exhausted (msk_depth != 0) and the new pointer fails nla_ok(), reject the filter with -EINVAL. An exactly exhausted mask still skips the check, preserving exact-match behaviour for the remaining key attributes. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:29.881Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99112
items.title_ko: [CVE-2026-99112] Linux 커널 net/sched cls_flower: nla_next() 이후 mask 포인터 검증 누락
items.summary_ko: fl_set_enc_opt()는 nla_next()로 진행하는 mask 포인터를 검증하지 않는다. mask에 유효한 속성 하나와 잔여 바이트가 있거나 속성 길이가 정렬되지 않으면, msk_depth가 0이 아닌 값으로 다음 반복에 전달되어 depth 검사가 작동하지 않는다. 기존 nla_ok() 검사는 방금 소비된 포인터만 확인하며, mask 속성은 NL_VALIDATE_LIBERAL 옵션으로 검증되어 잔여 바이트는 경고만 발생한다.
items.content_ko: 원인은 fl_set_enc_opt()가 key의 중첩 터널 옵션 속성을 nla_for_each_attr()로 순회하면서 단일 mask 포인터를 nla_next()로 진행시키는 방식이다. 이 때문에 mask 커서가 mask 자신의 속성이 아니라 key 속성 수에 따라 움직인다. 커밋 c96adff956191(“cls_flower: call nla_ok() before nla_next()”)이 추가한 nla_ok()는 이미 소비된 포인터만 검증하고, nla_next()가 만든 다음 포인터는 검증하지 않는다. 그 결과 fl_set_geneve_opt() 등 이후 헬퍼에서 depth 검사가 작동하지 않을 수 있다. 본문은 취약점의 영향과 이후 처리 과정을 설명하는 대목에서 끊긴다.

M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 combines next-generation performance and powerful on-device AI in a portable design, empowering students, creatives, developers, and business professionals to take their workflows anywhere.

With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.”

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

items.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
items.content:
Defenders across the world face the burden of responding to yet another botched code-execution vulnerability, this time in boot-time firmware used by most of the world’s server vendors and data centers.

The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II , an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the “preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications.” Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft’s hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot , which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install other payloads that also run each time early in the boot process.

The parties that discovered CVE-2026-97631—Alex Matrosov of Anthropic and Dan Holmes of Google—had arranged for it to stay under wraps until a coordinated disclosure that was scheduled for January. AMI, a maker of motherboards and other hardware, published this pull request last month that detailed the vulnerability and included a code fix. Once the post came to the attention of the discovering parties, TianoCore Project members published a public advisory last week.

With publicly available patch code, it will be trivial for advanced hackers to learn how the vulnerability is triggered and to build working exploits. Further compounding the urgency, patching UEFI code vulnerabilities in millions of end devices sold and used by thousands of hardware makers and cloud providers is cumbersome and time-consuming. Word of the vulnerability comes six days after another botched disclosure, this one involving a critical code-execution vulnerability in the PHP programming language.

“This vulnerability in the ICMP parser of the EDK2 network stack is interesting in terms of how it affects the chain of trust and the broader ecosystem,” said HD Moore, creator of Metasploit and chief research officer at security firm Dragos. “An attacker intent on compromising a nearby endpoint or server could use this bug to hijack program flow at a point where the boot process still has access to sensitive components, like the endpoint’s TPM. This could be used to break disk encryption for cases where an attacker has short-term network access (and it would be even easier in a theft scenario).”

CVE-2026-97631 is a 16-year-old buffer overflow in the PXE-Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe), which is responsible for allowing servers, storage equipment, and other devices to boot using code downloaded from a local network. During this process—known as the pre-execution environment boot—the driver uses a network listener to monitor for ICMP errors. Because the driver doesn’t enforce a memory copy limit of 504 bytes, overwriting adjacent data, a malicious insider or a hacker who has gained low-level access to a local network can send an error message that appends code past this limit. The IUEFI module running on the CPU then becomes corrupted.

During network boot, the PXE Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe) keeps a receive request open for ICMP error messages and copies each received message into the fixed 504-byte field Mode.IcmpError of its private context structure. items.title: Small models, specific purposes
items.content:
This website uses cookies to ensure you get the best experience.

We use them to remember your preferences and analyze site traffic.

I want to see how much useful work I can get from a small language model running on my own laptop. I am choosing a Surface Laptop, 8th Edition , partly because battery life and portability matter to me, but also because I am curious about what I can build on a reasonably priced device.

There are machines better suited to some of these experiments. I could look at the NVIDIA-powered Surface Laptop Ultra , an M5 MacBook Pro , or a dedicated desktop AI machine such as NVIDIA's DGX Spark . There are different tradeoffs in each, but I am simply unwilling to spend extra money chasing local AI capability or make that workload the deciding factor in the laptop I buy.

I have written about bringing Visual Studio natively to Arm64 and building out the workloads around it . The interest then was in making Arm a useful place to do development, rather than relying on emulation. Now I want to explore what a small model could add to that development experience on the same machine.

The configuration I am choosing has a Snapdragon X2 Elite with 12 CPU cores, 32GB of memory, and a Qualcomm Hexagon neural processing unit (NPU) rated at up to 80 TOPS . I am choosing a 1TB SSD to give me room for model files, repositories, and indexes. The storage is separate from the memory available to run a model.

TOPS means trillions of operations per second. The NPU is designed to run supported AI workloads efficiently, but that number does not tell me how quickly a model will respond. I still need to establish whether the model and runtime I choose can use it.

I want to try models that can work with code and use tools while leaving enough of the machine available for development. Phi-4-mini-instruct is one candidate, with 3.8 billion parameters and support for function calling. Its size gives me a concrete starting point for thinking about what the laptop would need to run it.

Weight memory (GB) = parameters_in_billions * bits_per_parameter / 8

The model also needs working buffers and a cache for the context it retains, including instructions, repository code, and test results. For Phi-4-mini, one example cache configuration would need about 1.1GB at 8,192 tokens, or 4.3GB at 32,768 tokens, separate from the weights. Windows and my development tools need their share too, so 1.9GB of weights does not mean a 1.9GB application.

That calculation gives me a starting point, but I do not want to repeat a detailed memory exercise for every model I consider. I also have to consider that using 16 bits to store each weight, rather than 4, allows more numerical precision but increases the weight memory to about 7.6GB.

A model runtime should handle much of that setup. Foundry Local is one Microsoft option, with a curated catalog from which I can choose a model and let the software select a hardware-appropriate variant. That is different from a guarantee that it will fit comfortably alongside Visual Studio at the context length I want to use.

I currently have access to what are, for me, essentially free tokens. That is something of a cheat code, but the allowance could be reduced or removed. It makes experimenting easy today, without telling me much about what I could sustain independently. Working on DasBlog Core with a local model would let me explore that, while still using the hosted models where they help.

DasBlog gives me an existing application to work with, and one whose behavior I know well enough to evaluate the result. I could start by asking a local agent to trace how an old permalink resolves to a post, using the relevant code to explain its answer. items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-99111 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix data corruption with concurre
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99111 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix data corruption with concurrent writes and O_TRUNC cifs_do_truncate() flushes dirty pages with filemap_write_and_wait() and truncates the file on the server, but in the old code both operations ran without holding i_rwsem or invalidate_lock. A concurrent buffered write via netfs_perform_write() -- which only needs i_rwsem shared -- could dirty new pages after the flush but before the local truncation, and those pages would be silently discarded by cifs_setsize() -> truncate_pagecache(). Fix by acquiring inode_lock (exclusive i_rwsem) and filemap_invalidate_lock at the top of cifs_do_truncate(), so the entire flush-truncate-resize sequence is atomic with respect to: - buffered writes (blocked by exclusive i_rwsem, since netfs_start_io_write takes i_rwsem shared), - read page faults (blocked by exclusive invalidate_lock, since filemap_fault takes it shared), - writeback collection (blocked by netfs_wb_begin/netfs_wb_end around the server truncate and local resize, since netfs_writepages also acquires the wb lock). 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:29.053Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99111

items.summary_ko: Linux 커널 SMB 클라이언트의 cifs_do_truncate()는 기존 코드에서 잠금 없이 더티 페이지 플러시, 서버 측 truncate, 로컬 크기 조정을 수행했다. 이 사이에 발생한 버퍼드 쓰기로 새로 더럽혀진 페이지가 cifs_setsize()에서 버려질 수 있었다. 수정은 함수 시작 시 배타적 i_rwsem과 filemap_invalidate_lock을 획득해 전체 과정을 원자적으로 처리하도록 한 것이다. 원문에 적힌 CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA)이며 원격 악용 가능 여부는 False로 표시되어 있다.
items.content_ko: Linux 커널의 SMB 클라이언트(cifs)에서 cifs_do_truncate()가 더티 페이지를 플러시하고 서버에서 파일을 자르며 로컬 크기를 조정하는 과정이 기존 코드에서는 i_rwsem이나 invalidate_lock 없이 실행되었다. 그 사이 netfs_perform_write()를 통한 동시 버퍼드 쓰기가 새 페이지를 더럽힐 수 있었고, 이 페이지들은 로컬 truncate 과정에서 조용히 버려졌다. 수정은 함수 시작부에서 배타적 inode_lock(i_rwsem)과 filemap_invalidate_lock을 획득해 플러시, truncate, 크기 조정 전체를 버퍼드 쓰기, 읽기 페이지 폴트, 쓰기백 수집에 대해 원자적으로 만든다. 원문에는 CVSS 0.0(NA), 원격 악용 가능 여부 False로 표기되어 있다.

items.title: 1,447 emoji? We'll do it live
items.content:
One of the things you get to do after being laid off is a lot of reflection, but also to revisit all the old projects you used to contribute to.

One of them was Pidgin : “the universal chat client” .

The new Pidgin 3 app icon and a handful emoji

I designed the original emoticon set for version 2 and helped redesign the user interface when the project was renamed from Gaim after a legal dispute .

Meanwhile, after a huge rewrite , Pidgin 3 is making progress towards a first release and I’ve been helping out here and there with a new app icon and some status symbols for the development releases.

I’ve been meaning to start live streaming my weekly app icon work to share a look in the kitchen of the icon design process, but once I gathered the courage to start a test run, the experience wasn’t amazing.

I need something I can return to consistently without needing a new plan every time…

So why not create a base set of 1,447 emoji for Pidgin in GNOME -style exclusively live on stream ? What could go wrong?

Here’s the design file to keep me accountable, so I can’t sneakily make progress offline!

I’ll be chipping away at it a few times a week. Follow me on Twitch to get a notification when I go live. We’ll grab a cup of tea, put on some music, and get through the winter.

If you want to support my design work for Free and Open Source projects, I’m always looking for more sponsors .

Or a “ sub ” as the kids call it these days.

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: Researchers Uncover Signs of Massive Surveillance Operation on Starlink Users
items.content:
Discover-Tech, an Israeli advertising firm previously linked to the delivery of zero-click spyware, is the top bidder for Starlink ad impressions in 105 countries, according to a new report from Reuters. Researchers say it all points to a large-scale tracking effort aimed at users of SpaceX’s satellite internet service.

John Scott-Railton, a senior researcher at the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, posted on X that data from TrendAI suggest the existence of a “worldwide surveillance op targeting @Starlink users.”

Discover-Tech was previously named in Citizen Lab’s October 15th report as the buyer of ordinary-looking ads that delivered Candiru spyware to devices at Al Jazeera without any user interaction. Candiru is an Israeli mercenary spyware vendor (now rebranded as Integrity Labs) that develops tools capable of silently compromising phones and computers. In 2021, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security added Candiru to their trade restriction list, known as the Entity List , over concerns it supplied surveillance technology used against journalists, activists, and government officials.

Citizen Lab’s initial report on Discover-Tech and Candiru from a couple of weeks ago described the first public technical confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted advertising. The associated researchers said they identified at least 45 devices at Al Jazeera infected with Candiru spyware in 2024 and 2025. Citizen Lab used network logs to reconstruct a sequence in which devices contacted Discover-Tech infrastructure when advertisements loaded, followed within seconds by communications with a Candiru validation server.

Discover-Tech presented itself as a legitimate advertising company and maintained certified or approved vendor status with Google and IAB Europe from 2020 until earlier this month. Analysis of roughly four billion bidding records from March to June 2026 showed Discover-Tech placed about 3.77 billion bids and won roughly 442 million auctions. Ads carrying its script tags appeared across 75,373 Android and iOS apps and 120,768 websites.

The company spent about $109,000 during the period with no recorded conversions, which researchers cited as further evidence that the activity was not a commercial advertising business. Ads reached networks associated with NATO, the European Parliament, the U.S. Department of Defense, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court, according to Citizen Lab and a parallel investigation by the ad security firm Confiant.

As part of the response to the investigation, Google terminated Discover-Tech’s access to its ad exchange platforms, telling Citizen Lab it had blocked the company from bidding or serving ads across Google’s ecosystem. IAB Europe removed it from its Global Vendor List on October 8th.

On the same day Citizen Lab published its report, TrendAI released an analysis of an ad tech entity it labeled SHADOW-EARTH-79. The research examined advertising telemetry and found that the entity was the No. 1 winning bidder for ad impressions on Starlink traffic in 105 countries. It accounted for approximately 12.9% of winning advertisements in the Starlink sample, compared with a 2.6% baseline share across general traffic, a nearly fivefold over-representation and the highest lift among high-volume buyers.

The skew was especially pronounced in several specific countries. SHADOW-EARTH-79 captured 91.3% of observed Starlink wins in Argentina, 89.1% in the Philippines, and 82.6% in Japan. It was also the top bidder in Syria, Libya, Yemen, and South Sudan, and the No. 2 bidder in Afghanistan, markets where TrendAI noted that “the demand for legitimate Western advertising in sanctioned or active-conflict states is effectively zero.” Similar dominance appeared in Hungary, Israel, Egypt, Azerbaijan, and Venezuela.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99110 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix heap overflow in cifs_do_set_acl() cifs_set_acl() validates ACL size using posix_acl_xattr_size(): 4 + (count * 8) // 4-byte header + 8 bytes per ACE cifs_do_set_acl() then calls posix_acl_to_cifs() to write the CIFS wire format into the same buffer: 6 + (count * 10) // 6-byte header + 10 bytes per ACE An ACL that passes the xattr-based check in cifs_set_acl() can overflow the heap when posix_acl_to_cifs() writes the larger CIFS format. Validate the CIFS format size against the remaining buffer space and USHRT_MAX before converting--data_count is __u16, so sizes above USHRT_MAX truncate the on-wire packet length, causing the server to apply a partial ACL. Replace MaxDataCount = 1000 with min(CIFSMaxBufSize, USHRT_MAX). 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:28.239Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99110
items.title_ko: CVE-2026-99110: Linux 커널 SMB 클라이언트 cifs_do_set_acl()의 힙 오버플로 수정
items.summary_ko: cifs_set_acl()은 posix_acl_xattr_size() 기준(4+8n바이트)으로 ACL 크기를 검증하지만, cifs_do_set_acl()은 그보다 큰 CIFS 포맷(6+10n바이트)을 같은 버퍼에 기록한다. 이 차이 때문에 검증을 통과한 ACL이 힙 버퍼를 넘칠 수 있었다. 수정은 CIFS 포맷 크기를 남은 버퍼 공간과 USHRT_MAX에 대해 검증하고, MaxDataCount를 min(CIFSMaxBufSize, USHRT_MAX)로 바꾼다.
items.content_ko: cifs_set_acl()은 ACL 크기를 posix_acl_xattr_size()로 검증하며 헤더 4바이트와 ACE당 8바이트를 기준으로 삼는다. 그러나 cifs_do_set_acl()은 posix_acl_to_cifs()로 헤더 6바이트와 ACE당 10바이트의 CIFS 포맷을 같은 버퍼에 쓴다. 따라서 기존 검사를 통과한 ACL이라도 더 큰 CIFS 포맷으로 기록될 때 힙 오버플로가 생길 수 있었다. 수정은 변환 전에 CIFS 포맷 크기를 남은 버퍼 공간과 USHRT_MAX와 비교해 검증한다. data_count가 __u16이므로 USHRT_MAX를 넘는 크기는 패킷 길이를 잘라 서버가 부분 ACL만 적용하게 만들 수 있었다. 이를 막기 위해 MaxDataCount = 1000을 min(CIFSMaxBufSize, USHRT_MAX)로 바꾼다. 원문 게시일은 2026-10-28이며, CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA)으로 표기되어 있다.

items.content:
Did you know OBS or FFmpeg can go directly into a video conference? You configure everything,

so you control exactly the quality you are going to get. WHIP support means these tools

now speak the protocol of video conferencing.

Send them an angry email. Tell them you don't want their crappy

proprietary client. You want open standards that let you bring the tools

WHIP is an open standard for sending live video to a service using WebRTC.

Your provider gives you a server URL and a stream key, called a bearer token. Before to join a conference

call each client had to run custom code. That means FFmpeg/OBS would never be able to join.

A lack of control. Your browser is picking a bitrate, codec or resolution that doesn't match what you need.

OBS and FFmpeg let you choose your resolution, frame rate, bitrate, and codec.

You can tune those settings for the content you're sharing and the hardware and connection you have.

OBS Virtual Camera sends your OBS scene to the conferencing app as a webcam.

You can pick the layout of your stream, but the conferencing app still handles encoding.

See the OBS WHIP setup guide I try and keep it up to date.

I work on WHIP in OBS. I'm tired of shitty screenshares when it is easily fixed.
items.title_ko: OBS·FFmpeg를 WHIP으로 화상회의에 직접 연결하기
items.summary_ko: OBS와 FFmpeg는 WHIP 지원을 통해 화상회의에 직접 영상을 보낼 수 있게 되었다. 이를 통해 해상도, 프레임 레이트, 비트레이트, 코덱을 사용자가 직접 설정할 수 있다. 글쓴이는 WHIP을 OBS에 구현하는 작업을 하고 있다.
items.content_ko: OBS나 FFmpeg를 화상회의에 바로 연결할 수 있다는 점을 알고 있는가. WHIP 지원 덕분에 이 도구들은 화상회의에서 쓰는 프로토콜로 영상을 보낼 수 있다. WHIP은 WebRTC를 이용해 라이브 영상을 서비스로 보내는 개방형 표준이다. 서비스 제공자는 서버 URL과 스트림 키(베어러 토큰)를 준다. 기존에는 회의에 참여하려면 각 클라이언트가 전용 코드를 실행해야 했고, 그래서 FFmpeg나 OBS는 참여할 수 없었다. 브라우저는 필요한 것과 다른 비트레이트, 코덱, 해상도를 고를 수 있어 통제력이 부족하다. OBS와 FFmpeg에서는 해상도, 프레임 레이트, 비트레이트, 코덱을 직접 고를 수 있으며, 공유하는 콘텐츠와 장비, 연결 환경에 맞춰 조정할 수 있다. OBS 가상 카메라는 OBS 장면을 회의 앱에 웹캠으로 보낸다. 스트림 레이아웃은 정할 수 있지만 인코딩은 여전히 회의 앱이 맡는다. 글쓴이는 OBS WHIP 설정 가이드를 최신 상태로 관리하고 있다고 적었다. 본문은 중간에 끊겨 있다.
