items.title: It Appears That the AI Bubble Has Just Burst in China
items.content:
As economists in the rest of the world look at the billions being poured into the AI industry with their hands over their eyes, the fate of China’s AI industry may be a sign of things to come.

A report from Reuters suggests that the AI bubble in China “has already burst.” Or it might be more apt to say that it shriveled like a rapidly deflating balloon: over the past four months, Reuters notes, the country’s STAR50 index of AI and semiconductor companies collapsed by 40 percent, wiping out $480 billion in market value. That is not a typo.

“The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull,” Beijing-based fund manager Dong Baozhen told Reuters . “And now we see the bubble bursting.”

Shares of Unitree, China’s buzzy robotics company , have halved since the company went public in a much-hyped IPO in August, the reporting noted. The chipmaker CXMT, meanwhile, has lost more than a quarter of its value over the past month.

The vicissitudes of the stock market haven’t completely dampened AI investors’ spirits, though. DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI companies, recently raised $15 billion in one of the largest funding rounds in the country’s history, Bloomberg reported . The outlet also noted that Huawei clinched a $2.3 billion loan from Chinese banks to spend on more AI chips.

The conditions in China, of course, are different than elsewhere in the world. China faces constant efforts from the US to ice it out of global competition, with tariffs and the US considering an outright ban on Chinese companies supplying equipment to data centers, such as Zhongji Innolight, whose optical transceivers are critical for facilitating the light-speed transfers of the epic amounts of data that AI requires. It’s worth noting that the role of the economic hostility by the US and other western countries in the Chinese market downturn could be being understated, with the downturn as much a consequence of China being blocked from selling its AI products overseas as much as it is of market arrogance.

Still, the scale of money being poured into AI and AI-related industries — with AI stocks taking up some 42 percent of China’s market capitalization, according to Goldman Sachs  — isn’t too dissimilar to what’s happening in Western economies, where the obvious lack of a return of investment becomes harder to ignore. Anthropic’s recent disclosure in its IPO filing of a staggering $80 billion loss — and plans to spend another $1 trillion on data centers over the next decade — will only further fuel fears that even the industry’s top players are still far from being profitable.

According to Reuters , state-backed investors sold into market rallies, or periods of rapid gains, to keep those gains in check, as part of a push by the government to dampen volatility. However intentioned that tactic may have been, it couldn’t dress up the fact that the demand for AI products just isn’t there yet.

items.title: KDE Fixes 15 Year Old Bug Over Inaccurate Notifications When Copying Files To USB Drives
items.content:
KDE Fixes 15 Year Old Bug Over Inaccurate Notifications When Copying Files To USB Drives

Written by Michael Larabel in KDE on 27 October 2026 at 12:50 PM EDT. 18 Comments

A long-standing KDE bug is set to be resolved with next month's KDE Frameworks 6.32 release.

Opened up in 2011 was this bug report around inaccurate notifications on the KDE desktop when copying files to a removable USB flash drive. The completion progress and complete notification only reflect copying to the local cache and not when the data is actually written out to the removable storage. Thus the KDE desktop would imply a file or files are already copied to a USB flash drive when in fact they have not been necessarily written out yet.

KDE developer Méven Car wrote an interesting KDE blog post today about this 15 year old bug report that saw 77+ comments and 17+ duplicate bug reports. Even with the current KDE Plasma stable releases, there still are these notifications not actually accurate about reporting true file completion on successfully completing copies to removable storage.

Coming up with a proper solution for accurately conveying when a file copy is completed to USB storage ended up being a very long and non-trivial process for KDE:

"The right tool actually showed up very early. Two days after the report, Christoph Feck asked whether there was a way to learn when the data is really on the disk "without causing massive slow downs that any sync type calls would cause". Two weeks later, the reporter passed on Alan Stern's answer, sync_file_range(), and Christoph replied that it looked like "exactly what we need". That was September 2011, and it is the call KIO now uses.

Then not much happened for years, apart from users confirming it and seventeen duplicates. In 2021, Nate Graham raised it to the highest priority, because a move deletes the source files while the copies are still in memory. In 2022, he changed the Disks & Devices applet, so that ejecting a device explains that it is still writing. In 2024, Christoph tested the cachestat() call of Linux 6.5, which reports how much of a file is still dirty in memory, but only for one file at a time.

This bug has been my white whale. I have been contributing to KIO since 2018, and I am still learning how the Linux storage stack behaves underneath it. I tried twice in 2024 and did not get sync_file_range() right. In MR 1718, the sync_file_range() path stayed commented out. In KIO MR 1764 and Dolphin MR 862, the worker waited for the writeback of the chunk it had just written, which had not started, so it never waited at all. Waiting for the window before the one just written is what makes it work. I didn't spot the issue, nor any reviewer unfortunately.

Since then, another contributor proposed turning off the cache for copies, in MR 2162, which was closed."

With KDE Frameworks 6.32, the completion dialog will now accurately reflect when the data is copied to the USB storage by making use of the sync_file_range() call.

Those curious about this lengthy adventure for fixing this 15 year old bug report can find all the technical details on the KDE.org blog .

items.content_ko: 2011년에 열린 이 버그 보고서는 KDE 데스크톱에서 이동식 USB 플래시 드라이브로 파일을 복사할 때 진행률과 완료 알림이 실제 기기에 쓰기가 끝난 시점이 아니라 로컬 캐시 기준으로 나타나는 문제를 다룬다. 그 결과 파일이 아직 기기에 완전히 기록되지 않았는데도 복사가 끝난 것처럼 보였다. 보고서에는 77개 이상의 댓글과 17건 이상의 중복 보고가 달렸다. 현재 KDE Plasma 안정 버전에서도 이 알림이 실제 완료 상태를 정확히 알려주지 못한다고 한다. 원문은 정확한 완료 시점을 알리는 해결책을 찾는 일이 까다로웠다고 전한다. 원문이 잘려 있어 구체적 구현 내용은 확인할 수 없다.

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-99109 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: reject SetEA requests that do not
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99109 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: reject SetEA requests that do not fit the request buffer CIFSSMBSetEA() copies the caller's extended attribute value into the SMB request buffer without checking that it fits. The requirement is stated in the source but was never implemented: /*BB add length check to see if it would fit in negotiated SMB buffer size BB */ /* if (ea_value_len > buffer_size - 512 (enough for header)) */ if (ea_value_len) memcpy(parm_data->list.name + name_len + 1, ea_value, ea_value_len); The only bound applied on the way in is in cifs_xattr_set(): #define MAX_EA_VALUE_SIZE CIFSMaxBufSize ... if (size > MAX_EA_VALUE_SIZE) CIFSMaxBufSize is the full payload capacity of the buffer, so a value of exactly that size leaves no room for the SMB header, the TRANS2 parameter block, the fealist header and the EA name that are written ahead of it in the same object. SendReceive() already enforces the correct limit on this very length: if (in_len > CIFSMaxBufSize + MAX_CIFS_HDR_SIZE) but it is called after the copy has taken place. An unprivileged setxattr(2) on an SMB1 mount with a 250-byte name and a 16384-byte value writes 16384 bytes starting 345 bytes into a 16588-byte cifs_request object, ending 141 bytes past it: BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in CIFSSMBSetEA+0xabc/0xde0 Write of size 16384 at addr ffff888003aa0159 by task init/68 __asan_memcpy+0x3c/0x60 CIFSSMBSetEA+0xabc/0xde0 cifs_xattr_set+0xd3a/0xff0 __vfs_setxattr+0x13e/0x1a0 The buggy address is located 345 bytes inside of allocated 16588-byte region Apply SendReceive()'s limit to the assembled request before the copy rather than after it, and widen the byte counters so the sum cannot wrap before it is tested. byte_count is also tested against U16_MAX, because it is stored in the 16-bit pSMB->ByteCount. That becomes reachable when CIFSMaxBufSize is raised at module load, where it may be set as high as 1024*127: with a 5-byte EA name and a 65521-byte value, count is exactly U16_MAX while byte_count is 65556, and cpu_to_le16() would truncate it to 20 and transmit a frame whose ByteCount does not match its length. Testing byte_count covers count as well, since byte_count is the larger of the two and count's only 16-bit consumer is written after this point. check_add_overflow() is evaluated first so that total_len is assigned before it is reported. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:27.507Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99109
items.title_ko: CVE-2026-99109: Linux 커널 SMB 클라이언트, 요청 버퍼에 맞지 않는 SetEA 요청 거부하도록 수정
items.summary_ko: CIFSSMBSetEA()는 호출자가 준 확장 속성 값을 SMB 요청 버퍼에 크기 검사 없이 복사했다. 소스 주석에만 있고 구현되지 않았던 길이 검사가 문제였으며, cifs_xattr_set()의 상한도 헤더 등을 고려하지 않은 CIFSMaxBufSize여서 부족했다. 본문은 권한 없는 사용자의 영향을 설명하는 부분에서 끊겨 있다.
items.content_ko: CIFSSMBSetEA()는 확장 속성(EA) 값을 SMB 요청 버퍼에 memcpy로 복사하는데, 복사 전에 그 값이 버퍼에 들어가는지 확인하지 않는다. 소스 주석에는 '협상된 SMB 버퍼 크기에 들어가는지 길이 검사를 추가할 것'이라는 내용이 있었지만 구현되지 않았다. 입력 단계의 유일한 제한은 cifs_xattr_set()에서 값 크기를 CIFSMaxBufSize와 비교하는 것인데, 이 값은 버퍼 전체 용량이라 SMB 헤더, TRANS2 파라미터 블록, fealist 헤더, EA 이름이 들어갈 공간을 남기지 않는다. 따라서 정확히 그 크기의 값은 같은 객체의 앞부분 데이터를 넘어 쓸 수 있었다. SendReceive()에도 올바른 상한 검사가 있지만 복사가 이미 끝난 뒤에 호출된다. 본문은 권한 없는 사용자가 이를 악용하는 경우를 설명하는 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Tailscale SSH: Investigation and remediation update
items.content:
Tailscale SSH: Investigation and remediation update

We're investigating security vulnerabilities affecting Tailscale SSH and wanted to share an update on what we've found, what we're doing about it, and what customers should know.

Our engineering and security teams have been investigating the reported issues with help from external security specialists. This builds on work already underway, which we've accelerated to address the findings and prepare fixes.

Most of the Tailscale SSH issues we've identified concern privilege escalation. In some circumstances, someone already authorized to connect over Tailscale SSH may be able to perform actions beyond the permissions of their configured local user, including potentially gaining elevated privileges.

These are serious security issues, and we're treating them accordingly.

Exploitation depends on the permissions granted to the connecting user or device, the system's configuration, and other conditions. We're continuing to verify the full scope of the findings and which configurations may be affected.

Based on our current assessment, we're not recommending that everyone disable Tailscale SSH.

Our engineers have implemented fixes for most of the issues identified and are completing testing ahead of a patched client release.

We're targeting a release by the end of Tuesday 27 October , subject to successful completion of testing. We'll update this page when the patched version is available, or if that timeline changes.

We're continuing to review the remaining findings and verify that our changes address the underlying problems.

While we're preparing the update, we recommend reviewing your Tailscale SSH configuration:

Review SSH access policies. Make sure access is limited to the users and devices that need it.

Disable SSH forwarding if you don't need it. Set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 in the tailscaled service environment and restart the service. This disables SSH forwarding without disabling Tailscale SSH entirely, and mitigates several of the more serious findings.

Review access to sensitive systems. Consider temporarily tightening your Tailscale SSH access policies while we investigate, so that only the specific users and devices that need access can connect.

Prepare to update. Apply the patched Tailscale client release when it becomes available.

Once the fixes are available, we'll publish a security advisory detailing the confirmed vulnerabilities, affected versions and configurations, their impact, and how to address them. We will link to that here when available.

We'll follow that with a technical blog post explaining the findings, the underlying causes, and the engineering changes we've made, again linked here when published.

If our assessment changes or we identify any additional steps customers need to take, we'll communicate those.

If you have questions about your particular environment, please contact Tailscale Support .

items.title: The Benchmarking Crisis
items.content:

optimizing for it, very much holds in database benchmarking. That is not

new, of course. Famously, TPC-D got retired when

people optimized so much for it that the query runtimes converged

towards zero due to excessive caching. TPC-H fixed that by

declaring itself to be an ad-hoc benchmark, and explicitly forbidding

things like exploiting knowledge about the workload or caching results

We now see the same problem with the ClickBench benchmark,

heavily accelerated by today’s use of AI code generation. If you tell an

AI to make the queries faster, it will make the queries faster,

regardless of whether this is a generally plausible approach or not. For

example, the pgrust implementation performs group-by aggregations on

string columns purely on the hash value, ignoring the long string

content. That is a great performance boost, of course, and works for

this benchmark, but can produce wrong results. Is it faster? Yes. Is it

a plausible optimization? Probably not. And it does many other things:

For example, ClickBench repeats certain predicates across queries, and

thus pgrust caches the predicate, completely eliminating the query cost

the second time. Or for query Q17, which returns tuples grouped by

userid, it makes use of the fact that a) tuples are roughly clustered by

userid, and b) the query specifies a limit clause without order by. Thus

any userid will do, and it never reads most of the data. A human would

not do these tiny micro-optimizations, because they are unlikely to be

relevant in general use cases, but an AI can of course look at each

Part of the problem is, of course, ClickBench itself. The benchmark

is not well specified in what is permitted and what is not, there is no

update stream, the queries are very simple, share predicates, are

underspecified, etc. But the fundamental problem is independent of that

concrete benchmark: The moment we start aggressively optimizing for a

specific benchmark, the benchmark stops being very useful. Historically,

that pressure was reduced a bit by the requirement that systems be

generally useful. That is, they did not just want to perform well in

benchmarks but also to be useful for their customers. That is, of

course, not a concern for vibe-coded execution engines.

It is not clear what to do about it. Our SQLStorm proposal tried

to address this by having tens of thousands of queries, which makes

overfitting harder. No human would fine-tune their system to such a huge

workload. But with AI tools we could even investigate ten thousand

queries in detail if needed, so that is not a real defense.

I think that to be meaningful, a benchmark has to a) like TPC-H, be

ad-hoc, and forbid exploiting prior knowledge and any form of

intermediate result caching. If we don’t do that, execution times

converge towards zero. And b) the benchmark has to include some form of

update stream, as otherwise overly aggressive read-only or read-mostly

systems will always outperform systems that offer full transactional

support. And c) the benchmark has to be truly ad-hoc, in the sense that

the systems tested have to be older than the benchmark. One way to fight

Goodhart’s law would be to (automatically) come up with a new benchmark

items.title_ko: 벤치마크의 위기
items.summary_ko: 측정 지표는 사람들이 그것을 최적화하기 시작하는 순간 쓸모를 잃는다는 법칙이 데이터베이스 벤치마크에도 그대로 적용된다고 주장한다. TPC-D는 캐싱으로 실행 시간이 0에 가까워져 폐기되었고, TPC-H는 워크로드 특성 활용과 결과 캐싱을 금지해 이를 막았다. 이제는 AI 코드 생성으로 ClickBench가 같은 문제를 겪고 있으며, pgrust 구현은 해시 값만으로 문자열 그룹 집계를 해 빠르지만 잘못된 결과를 낼 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 본문은 측정 지표가 최적화 대상이 되는 순간 쓸모를 잃는다는 법칙(앞부분이 잘려 있음)이 데이터베이스 벤치마킹에도 그대로 들어맞는다는 이야기로 시작한다. 과거 TPC-D는 사람들이 지나치게 최적화하면서 질의 실행 시간이 캐싱 때문에 0에 가까워져 폐기되었다. TPC-H는 스스로를 임시(ad-hoc) 벤치마크로 규정하고, 워크로드 지식을 활용하거나 결과를 캐싱하는 것을 명시적으로 금지했다. 글쓴이는 같은 문제가 ClickBench에서 AI 코드 생성의 확산으로 다시 나타난다고 지적한다. AI에게 질의를 빠르게 만들라고 하면, 그 방식이 일반적으로 타당한지와 상관없이 빠르게 만든다는 것이다. 예를 들어 pgrust 구현은 문자열 컬럼의 그룹 집계를 긴 문자열 내용은 무시하고 해시 값만으로 수행한다. 이 벤치마크에서는 빠르게 동작하지만 잘못된 결과를 낼 수 있다. 또 ClickBench는 여러 질의에서 같은 술어를 반복하는데, pgrust는 이를 캐싱한다고 한다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99108 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ntfs: fix FITRIM range alignment ntfs_trim_fs() aligns the start of a free extent up to the device discard granularity, but derives the discard length by aligning the original extent length down. When the free extent start is not discard-aligned, adding that length to the aligned start can extend the discard past the free extent and into allocated clusters. For example, with 4 KiB clusters and 32 KiB discard granularity, the free extent [4 KiB, 36 KiB) becomes the discard range [32 KiB, 64 KiB), so 28 KiB beyond the free extent may be discarded. Align the absolute end of the free extent down and derive the length from the two aligned endpoints. Skip extents that contain no full discard unit. Reproduced with a 4 KiB-cluster NTFS filesystem on scsi_debug configured for 32 KiB discard granularity and read-zero-after-trim. Before this change, FITRIM zeroed seven allocated 4 KiB clusters following an unaligned 32 KiB hole. With this change, the same data remains intact across FITRIM and remount. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-28T10:34:26.772Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-99108
items.title_ko: CVE-2026-99108: Linux 커널 NTFS FITRIM 범위 정렬 수정
items.summary_ko: ntfs_trim_fs()는 빈 공간 익스텐트의 시작점을 discard 단위에 맞춰 올림하면서도 길이는 원래 길이를 내림해 계산해, 정렬되지 않은 시작점일 때 discard 범위가 빈 공간을 넘어 할당된 클러스터까지 확장될 수 있었다. 예를 들어 4KiB 클러스터와 32KiB 단위에서 빈 공간 [4KiB, 36KiB)가 [32KiB, 64KiB)로 잡혀 28KiB의 할당 데이터가 지워질 수 있었다. 수정은 빈 공간의 끝점을 내림 정렬하고, 정렬된 두 끝점으로 길이를 계산하며, 완전한 discard 단위가 없는 익스텐트는 건너뛴다.
items.content_ko: NTFS의 ntfs_trim_fs()는 빈 공간 익스텐트의 시작점을 장치의 discard 단위에 맞춰 올림하지만, 길이는 원래 길이를 내림해 계산했다. 시작점이 discard 단위에 맞지 않으면 정렬된 시작점에 길이를 더한 범위가 빈 공간을 넘어 할당된 클러스터까지 discard될 수 있었다. 원문 예시는 4KiB 클러스터, 32KiB discard 단위에서 빈 공간 [4KiB, 36KiB)가 [32KiB, 64KiB)로 바뀌어 빈 공간 밖의 28KiB가 지워질 수 있다는 것이다. 수정은 빈 공간의 절대 끝점을 내림 정렬하고, 두 정렬된 끝점으로 길이를 계산한다. 완전한 discard 단위를 포함하지 않는 익스텐트는 건너뛴다. 재현 환경은 4KiB 클러스터 NTFS와 32KiB discard 단위를 가진 scsi_debug 장치이며, 수정 전에는 FITRIM 후 할당된 4KiB 클러스터 7개가 0으로 지워졌다. 수정 후에는 FITRIM과 재마운트 후에도 데이터가 유지되었다. 원문 게시일은 2026-10-28이다.

items.title: Git for the US Code
items.content:
A programmer can point at any line of code and see who wrote it, when, and what the file looked like on any past day. A lawyer reading a federal statute usually cannot, at least not without an afternoon in the notes at the foot of the section. But why shouldn't they have the same, convenient system of record? It is especially relevant given that so much first-pass legal research now runs through language models, which are often unable to utilise the proper lineage of a law, handcuffing its ability to offer interpretation.

Outside the titles Congress has enacted as positive law, the code is only prima facie evidence of the law, and the Statutes at Large govern where the two differ. [ 1 ] The Office of the Law Revision Counsel publishes it as a series of release points, each current through a named public law, and keeps reorganising it; a bill to enact title 41 as positive law was introduced in September 2025. [ 2 ] Which public law wrote a sentence is recorded in amendment notes, in prose. When a change took effect is often in a separate effective-date note, and where Congress said nothing the default rule is that a law takes effect on the day it is enacted. [ 3 ]

The definition of a small business debtor in 11 USC § 1182(1) shows how far apart those answers can be. It was created in 2019 with the existing small business debt limit. [ 4 ] The CARES Act raised the limit to $7.5 million in March 2020 as a temporary measure, later extended to March 2022. [ 5 ] , [ 6 ] That increase lapsed on 27 March 2022, and on 21 June 2022 Congress restored it for two more years, for cases commenced on or after 27 March 2020 and still pending, which reached back over the gap. [ 7 ] The higher limit expired again in June 2024, and after the triennial adjustment in April 2025 it stands at $3,424,000. [ 8 ] , [ 9 ] For a case filed in May 2022, the release point printed at the time gives the lower limit, and only a later Act changes the answer. A history that is useful to a lawyer has to carry the text, the date each change took force, and the scope of any law that reaches back.

A study from the Technical University of Munich this year found two failures in models answering questions on German statutes: they apply rules that were superseded after their training cutoff, and they prefer the newer provision even when an older one governs the facts. One model answered 24% of post-cutoff questions correctly on its own and 87% when the relevant statutory text was retrieved for it, and the authors conclude that temporal validity has to be treated as a hard constraint. [ 10 ] Other recent work trains search agents to respect the date a question is about, with large gains in consistency. [ 11 ]

Asking a model to produce the old text does not solve this. When the same Munich group had a model apply German amending laws to earlier versions, the output looked 93–99% similar to the official text, but only half of single amendments and a fifth of chains of amendments matched exactly, and experts found legally significant errors in the near misses. [ 12 ] The history has to be checkable.

For each pair of release points from 2017 onward, we took the public laws enacted in between, carried out their amending instructions on the older text in date order, and compared the result with the newer version. Of 365 changes across the nine titles, 361 reproduced the next release point exactly. The other four are shown with a label saying how far they could be confirmed. Each change then carries the law and the date it took effect: 261 took effect on enactment by default, 72 by an effective-date note and 29 by a date in the amendment itself. One depends on an agency determination that may never come, and we leave it out of the text rather than guess.

With that record, the reader can answer the questions lawyers ask. You pick a date and get the text in force on it, with the words that read differently today marked. Each phrase is coloured by the Act that wrote it. A…
items.title_ko: 미국 법전을 위한 Git
items.summary_ko: 프로그래머는 코드의 각 줄을 누가, 언제, 어떤 내용으로 바꿨는지 추적할 수 있지만 변호사는 연방 법령에서 그렇게 하기 어렵다고 글쓴이는 지적한다. 법률 조사에 언어 모델이 많이 쓰이는 지금, 법령의 연혁을 제대로 파악하지 못하면 해석 능력이 떨어진다는 문제도 있다. 본문은 미국 법전의 개정 기록 방식과 효력 발생일 규칙을 설명하며, 이를 Git처럼 추적 가능한 체계로 만드는 필요성을 주장한다.
items.content_ko: 프로그래머는 코드의 어느 줄이든 누가 언제 썼는지, 과거 어느 날 파일이 어떤 모습이었는지 볼 수 있다. 반면 연방 법령을 읽는 변호사는 조문 아래 주석을 한참 뒤져야 하는 경우가 많다. 글쓴이는 법률 조사에 언어 모델이 많이 쓰이는 지금, 법령의 연혁을 제대로 다루지 못하는 것이 해석 능력을 제한한다고 본다. 미국 법전에서 의회가 정식 법률로 제정한 편을 제외하면 법전은 법의 표면적 증거일 뿐이며, 차이가 있을 때는 Statutes at Large가 우선한다. 법률 자문관실(Office of the Law Revision Counsel)은 법전을 특정 공법까지 반영된 릴리스 단위로 공개하며 계속 재편하고 있다. 2025년 9월에는 제41편을 정식 법률로 제정하려는 법안이 발의되었다. 어떤 문장을 어느 공법이 썼는지는 개정 주석에 설명 형태로 기록되며, 효력 발생 시점은 별도의 효력일 주석에 있다. 의회가 시점을 정하지 않은 경우 법은 제정된 날 효력이 발생한다는 기본 규칙이 적용된다. 본문은 정의 조항 설명 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Instagram Meta AI Vulnerability: How Hackers Bypassed 2FA with Prompt Injection
items.content:
Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. items.title: Some Google Home Speakers downloading massive amounts of data in the background
items.content:
The new Google Home Speaker has an issue where it downloads hundreds of gigabytes of data in the background for some owners.

Over the past week, several reports have emerged about how the Google Home Speaker appears to be continuously downloading data from company servers.

In my case, a Google Home Speaker that has not been used in the past day for voice commands or media streaming consumed 17 GB of data in 24 hours. At 3 a.m. PT, it downloaded 9.99 GB. Given the timing, this could be related to failed attempts to download device firmware.

Meanwhile, on October 13, the same speaker downloaded 41 GB of data. Over the past 30 days, the total download comes in at 132 GB.

It’s not clear if this is a widespread issue. Another lightly used Home Speaker of ours (in a different household) downloaded only 2 GB of data in the past month.

That doesn't make sense how much storage does it have? It's just downloading and deleting constantly?

Most routers let you check how much data a particular device has used. If you’re using Nest Wifi, go to the Google Home app’s Wifi top tab > Devices > select your speaker > Device usage graphs. You can switch between 1-, 7-, and 30-day graphs.

We’re not seeing this download issue with other Google Home and Nest devices, including several Nest Hubs in the same house as the affected Home Speaker.

If you have multiple Home Speakers and a limited data plan, this issue could easily breach your cap, as some have found.

In a statement to 9to5Google today, the company acknowledged the issue and said “a fix is already rolling out that should address this for users.”

items.title: Ink droplets in motion snag top prize in Nikon Small World contest
items.content:
A 25-year-old German experimental photographer has won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition with a striking image of droplets of ink being deposited on paper by an inkjet printer. Ole Bielfeldt beat out 1,802 other entries hailing from 69 different countries.

Bielfeldt became interested in photomicrography during the COVID-19 lockdown after discovering an old microscope in his parents’ attic. He figured out how to build an adaptor out of a tube and some wood to connect the microscope to his father’s camera and taught himself the art through trial and error, building custom tools as needed. He documents how he captures transformative images of everyday objects with behind-the-scenes videos posted to macrofying , his photography and videography brand.

It was Bielfeldt’s curiosity about the inner workings of inkjet printers that inspired his winning entry, but capturing the action of ink drops being deposited on paper was a challenge, given that the process happens so quickly. The droplets, for instance, moved faster than the camera’s shutter speed. Bielfeldt’s solution was to deconstruct the printer so that the paper moved under a stationary (rather than moving) printhead, and then take the image in a dark room, using a flash to serve as the shutter, thereby freezing the ink drops mid-air. There was no need for pricey equipment. Bielfeldt does not use AI in his images, preferring to rely on traditional techniques.

“Ole Bielfeldt’s winning image embodies what makes Nikon Small World so powerful: the intersection of microscope imaging, ingenuity, and artistry,” said Eric Flem , a spokesperson for Nikon Instruments. “By using a microscope objective in a different way, he transformed a familiar object into something altogether new and previously unseen. It is a reminder that the microscope is not only a scientific tool but also a creative one, capable of expanding how we see and imagine the world around us.”

Founded in 1974, the Nikon Small World competition celebrates its 52nd anniversary this year. In 2011, the company added the Small World in Motion competition (see the 2026 winner here ). Both are meant “to showcase the beauty and complexity of things seen through the light microscope”—one through still photographs, the other through photovideography, taking advantage of all the technological advances that now allow users to make movies or time-lapse images through the microscope.

Here are the top 10 winners of this year’s competition; the full list, with honorable mentions, can be found here . Nikon is also producing a full-color 2027 calendar featuring the 2026 winners.

Microscopic view of an inkjet printer depositing ink on paper.

Microscopic view of an inkjet printer depositing ink on paper.

Hemitrichia slime mold spore structure (fruiting bodies).

Human neurons reprogrammed from skin cells growing in a microfluidic chamber.

Pencil lead during exposure to a high-voltage electrical discharge.

De-differentiated liver endothelial cell.

A parasitoid wasp emerging from a butterfly chrysalis.

Jennifer is a senior writer at Ars Technica with a particular focus on where science meets culture, covering everything from physics and related interdisciplinary topics to her favorite films and TV series. Jennifer lives in Baltimore with her spouse, physicist Sean M. Carroll, and their two cats, Ariel and Caliban.

items.title: Compile-Time Dependent Types
items.content:
It seems inevitable that compile-time dependent types will come to systems programming.

C++ has templates and constexpr . Rust has const generics. Zig has comptime . Even C has _Generic .

However, these features tend to be highly restricted, lack a proper type system, or both.

I’m working on Syl , a language which aims to encode compile-time computation in a modal type system.

Syl is primarily inspired by András Kovács’ work on two-level type theory , as well as plans for OxCaml .

The Syl compiler may be found on GitHub .

In Syl, all values have a mode along with a type.

Modes describe properties of values independent of their types.

For example, OxCaml uses modes to indicate whether a value is uniquely owned, may be written to, may be sent to another thread, etc. 1

Syl has two mode axes: staticity and erasure .

On the staticity axis, a value may be either static or dynamic .

For example, literals are static unerased , since they are clearly knowable at both compile time and runtime.

You can check by writing a mode annotation:

Each mode axis has a sub-moding relation.

If you have a static value, it’s safe to forget that it is knowable at compile time and hence treat it as dynamic .

Similarly, an unerased value may be treated as erased .

Mode annotations may “weaken” the mode, but not “strengthen” it:

As you might expect, branching on a dynamic value causes the result to be dynamic .

As long as they don’t capture or branch on dynamic values, functions preserve staticity. 2

Functions that return erased values are themselves erased , so cannot be applied at runtime.

Now, what can we do with this information?

When a value is knowable at compile time, surrounding code can be monomorphized .

Functions of static parameters take advantage of this fact:

Whenever we call f x , the compiler requires that both f and x have mode static .

If they do, it selects a particular implementation of f specialized to the value of x .

Concretely, f true would call a function that hard-codes print_bool true , and likewise for f false .

In this example, we’re printing the value of x at runtime, so it needs to be unerased .

That’s often unnecessary: if x only determines how to compile the body of f , it can be erased .

Here, erased also implies static , so f will be specialized on x .

The if erased expression accepts a static erased condition and is guaranteed to resolve at compile time.

Therefore, the body of f true is simply print_int 0 , and likewise for f false .

On their own, the static and erased modes let us explicitly request specialization-based optimizations,

but they don’t give us dependent types. Functions of static arguments do.

Here, if erased allows us to return an integer if x is true and a boolean otherwise.

Hence, f has a dependent function type, which encodes how the result type depends on the value of the input.

Note ty as name gives the argument a name for use in the result.

Applications can then determine the correct result type by evaluating f ’s type.

There is no distinct type grammar: type formers like -> and type annotations are normal expressions.

int  and  bool are just erased values of type type , and abstracting over them gives us polymorphism.

As we saw above, functions of static arguments are monomorphized.

At runtime, id int refers to an identity function that directly operates on integers, and likewise for id bool .

That is, Syl is dependently typed at compile time and simply typed at runtime. 3

Constructs that determine the shape of the runtime program require static information.

Types are always erased , so the runtime program cannot inspect types.

Syl implements dependent typechecking similarly to existing languages, so we won’t discuss it in detail.

However, the relationship between types and propositions in Syl differs from that of languages like Lean, Rocq, and Agda.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: Police Are Using AI to Pull Over Drivers for ‘Suspicious’ Behavior
items.content:
Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) aren’t just helping police investigate crimes anymore. They’re now being used to flag drivers for supposedly “suspicious” driving patterns.

The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) sounded the alarm Monday in a blog post on Monday, warning that law enforcement agencies across the United States are increasingly using license plate readers and AI-powered tools to pull over drivers even if they aren’t suspected of having committed a specific crime.

The post opens with the story of Grace Knowles, a woman in her 20s from northern Virginia who took a road trip through Oregon, Texas, and Louisiana in September 2025. On her way to Florida, she was pulled over by an officer who claimed she had spent too much time driving in the left lane.

The officer questioned Knowles about her travels and asked for proof that she had been in New Orleans. He eventually identified himself as a special agent with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) that was on a project for human and drug trafficking. He told her that her license plate had been flagged for suspicious travel patterns.

After she convinced him she was just on a road trip, he offered to show her what he was looking at on a computer in his car.

“It was basically a heat map of the U.S., and I could see different circles where I’d been, and when he clicked on it, it was a photo of my license plate,” Knowles told the ACLU.

When she asked how authorities had collected images of her license plate, the officer told her the cameras were everywhere, including on top of highway signs.

The ACLU warns that encounters like Knowles’ could become more common.

“For many people, those encounters will be far more fraught, frightening and dangerous than what Knowles experienced,” wrote Jay Stanley, a senior policy analyst with the ACLU.

ALPRs facing growing pushback nationwide

The warning comes as ALPRs are already facing growing backlash.

Companies like Flock Safety and Axon have become known in recent years for selling ALPR systems to law enforcement, which scan license plates as vehicles pass, collecting vehicle information along with the time and location they were spotted. Police can then search that data during investigations.

Privacy advocates, however, warn that the cameras collect location data on millions of people who are not suspected of crimes, often without a warrant, probable cause, or reasonable suspicion. There have also been reports of the systems leading to mistakes and rampant misuse by law enforcement.

An August YouGov survey found that 46% of respondents opposed law enforcement using the technology in their communities, while 38% supported it.

Law enforcement agencies around the country, including the Los Angeles Police Department , have suspended or even ended their Flock contracts amid the growing backlash.

Knowles’ story is far from the only case raising concerns about how police are using license plate data.

In March, The Markup reported that a California grandmother was questioned by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CPB) officers about how often she visited local casinos. In another case , a man was targeted for a traffic stop after repeatedly driving back and forth between Wisconsin and Michigan, which local police described as “a known source State for Marijuana.”

Earlier this month, a federal jury in Texas sided with a man who sued over what his attorneys described as an “unconstitutional traffic stop scheme” enabled by “AI-powered” license plate readers. According to the lawsuit, he was pulled over after his license plate was flagged for driving from Houston to Carrizo Springs, staying overnight, and returning home the following day.

Meanwhile, WIRED reported this month that Flock had developed an AI-powered investigative tool that “can identify drivers and track vehicles by their patterns of movement alone.”

Flock did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Updated PHP Windows builds for Brotli security fix
items.content:
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately.

Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.

RCE via OOM corruption , CVE-2026-109618 ( GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w ): out-of-memory

handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.

RCE via stale global state , CVE-2026-109619 ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ): request-owned

internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.

Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Source downloads are on our downloads page . Windows source and binaries are on the same page .

Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance, so check your vendor for updated packages.

PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version.

Given the severity of these vulnerabilities, the PHP security team provided minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4 , PHP 8.0 , and PHP 8.1 to help people building from source or without access to an LTS vendor.

If you cannot update immediately: while only an update is a complete solution, the following measures reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe.

RCE via OOM corruption (CVE-2026-109618):

Set memory_limit=-1 , preferably in a way applications can't override, such as php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration, and check that no pool, directory or application setting puts a finite limit back. This removes the controllable PHP memory limit failure, but an underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path.

Set a low post_max_size . For applications that don't require file uploads, set post_max_size = 8M . If file uploads are necessary, set post_max_size = 32M . Keep upload_max_filesize below post_max_size .

Consider enforcing limits at the web server or proxy level for decoded request size, input field count, multipart part count, header count, and nesting depth. These

limits must also cover requests without a usable Content-Length .

Use a container or cgroup limit as an availability boundary, preferably with a policy that kills only the affected worker. Do not substitute RLIMIT_AS or

RLIMIT_DATA , as these can cause the vulnerable allocation failure.

RCE via stale global state (CVE-2026-109619):

Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart every worker. Use php.ini , an FPM pool or server

configuration that applies before request parsing. Do not rely on ini_set() or FPM .user.ini . This blocks the confirmed session paths but not other variants.

On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart every worker. This blocks the confirmed fatal backtrace path only.

Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization. Hiding diagnostics with error_reporting , display_errors

Fix attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts, including failures in callbacks, upload or import processing and cleanup.

The advisories linked above have the full technical details.

items.content:

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-99106 📢 Source: Linux 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: free the userptr ranges when a CS fails after parser_bos amdgpu_cs_parser_bos() allocates an HMM range for every userptr entry of the BO list and looks up the user pages. Those ranges are only freed when amdgpu_cs_parser_bos() itself fails or when amdgpu_cs_submit() checks them under the notifier lock. If amdgpu_cs_patch_jobs(), amdgpu_cs_vm_handling(), amdgpu_cs_sync_rings() or the early part of amdgpu_cs_submit() fails, nothing frees them: neither amdgpu_cs_parser_fini() nor amdgpu_bo_list_free() touch e->range. Each such CS then leaks the range, its hmm_pfns array (8 bytes per page of the userptr BO) and the BO reference the range holds. An IB on a ring that patches the CS in place (e.g. VCN) with an unmapped va_start fails in amdgpu_cs_patch_ibs() and takes this path. Free the ranges on those error paths. Ranges amdgpu_cs_submit() already dropped are NULL, so freeing them again is a no-op. items.summary_ko: Linux 커널 amdgpu 드라이버에서 amdgpu_cs_parser_bos() 이후 CS(명령 제출)가 실패하면 userptr의 HMM 범위가 해제되지 않아 메모리 누수가 발생할 수 있었습니다. 누수 대상은 범위 구조체, hmm_pfns 배열, 그리고 범위가 보유한 BO 참조입니다. 수정은 해당 오류 경로에서 범위를 해제하도록 하는 것이며, 원래 커밋은 c52a9542ed7cfd527feb938bd0accada2ac8d267입니다.
items.content_ko: Linux 커널 amdgpu 드라이버에서 amdgpu_cs_parser_bos()가 userptr BO 목록의 각 항목에 HMM 범위를 할당하고 사용자 페이지를 조회합니다. 하지만 이 범위는 amdgpu_cs_parser_bos() 자체가 실패하거나 amdgpu_cs_submit()이 알림 잠금 아래에서 확인할 때만 해제됩니다. 따라서 amdgpu_cs_patch_jobs(), amdgpu_cs_vm_handling(), amdgpu_cs_sync_rings() 또는 amdgpu_cs_submit() 초반부가 실패하면 범위가 해제되지 않아, 범위, hmm_pfns 배열(userptr BO 페이지당 8바이트), 범위가 쥐고 있는 BO 참조가 누수됩니다. 예를 들어 VCN처럼 CS를 제자리에서 패치하는 링의 IB에서 va_start가 매핑되지 않으면 amdgpu_cs_patch_ibs()가 실패하며 이 경로를 밟습니다. 수정은 이 오류 경로에서 범위를 해제하는 것이며, 이미 amdgpu_cs_submit()에서 해제된 범위는 NULL이므로 다시 해제해도 문제가 없습니다. 공개일은 2026-10-28입니다.
